Is depression legally protected like physical disorders. Ive been diagnosed with depression, and my depression is the kind that manifests itself as severe apathy with a side of anxiety. Anyway, this causes a punctuality issue. Im almost always late to everything, and this has caused issues at work. Ive lost previous jobs due to it, and Ive been put on notice at my current job. Its not much. Over the course of a five day week Ill be a total of around 10 minutes of tardiness. Some days might be 5+ minutes, but usually Im on time a couple days and 13 minutes other days. I consider a few minutes to be so insignificant an amount of time as to not even bother considering. I cant bring myself to care about it, and the idea of being punished for such a small amount of tardiness, considering I otherwise do an excellent job at my work, infuriates me. I have a coworker with a medical disorder who is completely unreliable. Shes missed at least three months of work each year since Ive been here due to her medical issues, but my manager cant punish her or file administrative action because medical issues are legally protected. I havent told my manager that Ive been officially diagnosed with depression because it just happened yesterday, and because Im pretty sure no manager wants to hear me say something along the lines of I am emotionally incapable of caring about you, this job, or being on time. Is depression similarly protected? If so, does anyone know how I can successfully challenge my current administrative action?

Will I ever be rid of it. Hey guys, m22 here with OCD. I was diagnosed when I was 12 yo. My 10th year of dealing with OCD has been a pain in the butt. For many years I thought that the worst was over. I used to have intensely obsessive thinking. I have POCD, HOCD, and PureO. I have been in and out of therapy for years, and I have had enough prozac to give an elephant a cocaine overdose over the span of several years, Im not a drug addict. I just graduated from college and I am finally in a full time job. I thought that life was going great until about 6 months ago. Not only was I hit with depression out of nowhere, but I also started to realized that my OCD had been creating invisible problems for me for years. Thoughts, ideas, and even my concept of religion suddenly stopped making sense. It was like my OCD was acting on its own volition to screw up my life behind my back. I started seeing my therapist again, and my life isnt that bad. Im still really frustrated though because I am finally realizing that OCD will never leave me alone. I will always be dealing with my screwed up brain, and all I can do is keep fighting. After 10 years of fighting my OCD, I have realized that it cant be defeated, only put to sleep. Any thoughts on this? Any similar experiences? I am willing to answer any questions as well, Im an open book.

I cant wait until stress is looked at as a serious health concern. Ongoing stressor may result in chronically elevated blood pressure and hypertension. Now, although having a chronic stress condition isnt listed under high risk factors for hypertension heart attacks it is considered a risk factor. Stress, is considered a risk factor for hypertension which can lead to heart attacks as well as strokes, kidney disease, diabetes, angina pectoris a.k.a chest chain, etc. WHY then, is stress not taken seriously? As someone who suffers from anxiety, depression and PTSD I get inconvenienced by stress physically every day. This is a huge concern of mine, and the anxiety only further contributes to more stress over having a stroke or heart attack especially since I have a family history of cardiovascular disease.
